Precarious

prih-KAIR-ee-us -- shares a root with 'pray,' from a Latin word meaning obtained by begging. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Precarious is not securely held or positioned; dangerously likely to fail or fall.

The climber found herself in a precarious position, clinging to a ledge that could crumble at any moment.

Worked Example

A stack of dinner plates teeters on the very edge of a table, wobbling every time someone walks past, with nothing holding it in place.

That unstable, about-to-fall quality is exactly what precarious describes. Unlike 'secure,' which means firmly fixed, precarious means one small nudge away from disaster.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shaky: unsteady or likely to fail

unstable: not firmly fixed; likely to change or fail

perilous: full of danger or risk

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

stable: firmly fixed and not likely to change or fail

secure: firmly fixed and protected from danger

Where it sits · how serious the danger becomes — shaky → precarious → perilous

shaky vs. precarious: Shaky is a more everyday word than precarious -- shaky can describe something simply wobbly or uncertain, while precarious specifically emphasizes real danger of a sudden fall or failure.

perilous vs. precarious: Perilous can feel stronger than precarious: precarious emphasizes instability and the risk of falling, while perilous broadens that danger to include any serious risk to safety, not just balance.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — -prec-

root — -prec-: to pray, beg (Latin (precari))

suffix — -arious

suffix — -arious: full of, connected with (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin precari meant 'to pray or beg,' and -arious means 'full of, connected with' -- precarious originally described something held only by another's goodwill, granted because you begged for it. Anything resting on such shaky support can be lost at any moment.

Word Choice

Precarious can describe a physical position, like a ledge or stack of objects, or a figurative situation, like a precarious financial state or a precarious peace agreement.
